title: Record intervention kind; count only rescues in sensor and scores
summary: Add a required-at-write "kind" to intervention records (rescue, audit-finding, custody), set by `athena intervene`. The scorer's p_user_intervenes outcome and the intervention sensor and counts then use only rescues. This is for the Athena owner, who reads these counts to judge what Athena could not do.

defaults_applied.how: New tests cover scoring, the CLI flag, and legacy loading. Criteria require cargo test and clippy to be clean.
Criteria check that scores and records change by kind, not that the enum exists.
Every consumer of interventions is audited, not just the scorer.
Docs and the changelog define the three kinds.
One focused additive field with a default; no schema bump.
The verifier runs cargo test, clippy, and fmt --check.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Kind is a new field on athena.intervention/1 (InterventionKind: rescue, audit-finding, custody), separate from the existing eight-way category, which says how the user helped.
Existing records are immutable and lack the field, so a missing kind deserializes as rescue; this keeps history counted as before.
Observed interventions (a one-line correction of a reading) are rescues, since the user steered Athena.
athena intervene takes a --kind flag. It defaults to rescue when omitted, which is the old behaviour. Unknown values are rejected with the list of allowed values.
The scorer's `intervened` check (athena-score) and every other count that reads interventions use rescues only. Non-rescue records are still stored, shown in status as open work, and introspected.
This is not a schema-version bump: the field is additive with a default, so the schema name stays athena.intervention/1.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run `cargo test`: a new scoring test shows a job with only an audit-finding or custody intervention after dispatch scores intervened=false, and a job with a rescue scores intervened=true.

Run `cargo test`: a new CLI lifecycle test runs `athena intervene --kind custody` (and audit-finding). The written record's JSON contains the kind, and an invalid --kind fails with the allowed values listed.
Run `cargo test`: a record without a kind field still loads and counts as a rescue, and a round-trip serialization writes the kind.

Every place that counts or senses interventions (the scorer, the introspection trigger, status and backtest counts) is shown in the diff filtering on rescue. Any place that deliberately keeps counting all kinds is commented with why.
docs/records.md and CHANGELOG.md describe the three kinds, with a definition of each, the legacy default, and the rule that only rescues count.
Run `cargo clippy` and `cargo fmt --check`: both clean. `cargo test` passes for the whole workspace.

out_of_scope: Rewriting or backfilling existing records under records/ (they are immutable)
Changes to athena.toml, defaults.toml or workflows
Automatically classifying a kind from the text of what or why
departures: The change spans the data schema, the CLI, the scorer and several tests, so cost and time sit above the reference. The ambiguity over where to draw the line for counts adds some risk of rejection.
